verdict: Lightspeed Retail: Choose Lightspeed Retail when in-store POS and inventory are the system of record and the online store should follow that catalog — not when you only need an embeddable cart (Ecwid) or a free Square Online add-on. Scores use the Ecommerce editorial methodology from first-party research as of 2026-08-17 — not hands-on product testing.
strengths: True retail POS with inventory and omnichannel as the center of gravity
Published Basic / Core / Plus USD tiles
Lightspeed Payments card-present rate published around 1.5%
Built-in eCommerce on higher tiers (not a separate CMS migration)
weaknesses: Higher published floor than Square Online’s free tier
Third-party processor surcharge risk — confirm live
Not the Lightspeed embeddable-cart product (that is Ecwid)
bestFor: Brick-and-click retailers who need POS + inventory as the system of record
Multi-location specialty retail outgrowing Square’s simplest online store
Merchants who will use Lightspeed Payments rather than fight processor surcharges
notIdealFor: Online-only brands without a retail floor (see Shopify)
Existing-site owners who only need an embeddable cart (see Ecwid)
Teams standardized on Square hardware who want the cheapest online add-on
tradeoffs: Subscription floors vs payment-processing spreads and GMV/overage fees
App/extension TCO vs native feature depth
Open-source/hosting flexibility vs SaaS operational simplicity
Dropshipping product caps vs catalog automation depth
recommendation: Choose Lightspeed Retail when in-store POS and inventory are the system of record and the online store should follow that catalog — not when you only need an embeddable cart (Ecwid) or a free Square Online add-on. Consider Square Online if you already run Square POS and want the cheapest unified online store; Shopify for online-first scale with POS as an add-on; Ecwid if you only need to embed a cart on an existing site.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Retail POS admin is capable for store teams, with more onboarding than Square’s free-tier simplicity.
Scored as omnichannel retail (POS + online), not as a website builder or embeddable cart. Landscape peer — Square Online keeps the cluster award.
Inventory, variants, and multi-location catalog are Lightspeed Retail strengths versus Square’s simpler online catalog.
In-person checkout is the core; online checkout is solid on higher-tier eCommerce — not Shop Pay-class.
Accounting (QuickBooks/Xero), payments, and app connectors are strong for a retail POS suite.
This is the job — unified retail POS, inventory, and omnichannel selling. Distinct from Ecwid’s embeddable cart.
Core/Plus and multi-location packaging support growing retailers better than Square’s simplest online store.
$89 floor and possible third-party processor surcharges compress value versus Square’s free online entry — justified when POS depth is the purchase reason.
Limited first-party AI versus larger SaaS platforms — not a scoring driver.

overallScoreRationale: Weighted average of the nine ecommerce editorial criteria using category weights (storefront/commerce fit 15, catalog/orders 14, ease 12, checkout 12, integrations 12, value 12, omnichannel/POS 10, scalability 9, AI 6), rounded to 1 decimal. Products are scored inside their job cluster — SaaS platforms, open-source carts, omnichannel POS bundles, and dropshipping sourcing apps are not forced into one undifferentiated ranking. Not a hands-on lab score; affiliate economics are excluded.
